title: In vivo imaging of mitophagy in Caenorhabditis elegans
protocol: Prepare NGM plates.

Add 8-10 L4 larvae of transgenic animals expressing mtRosella or mtGFP together with the autophagosomal marker LGG-1 fused with DsRed in body wall muscle cells on a freshly E. coli (OP50) seeded NGM plate.
Incubate worms at 20°C.
Pick L4 transgenic animals to synchronize worm population.
Add 15-20 L4 transgenic animals per plate for each experimental condition, using at least three plates.
Transfer worms to freshly seeded NGM plates every two days to avoid progeny and prevent starvation due to lack of food.
Kill E. coli (OP50) bacteria seeded on NGM plates by UV irradiation for 15 min (0.5 J).
Add paraquat or CCCP to the top of seeded NGM plates at final concentrations of 8 mM and 15 μM in total agar volume, respectively.
Gently swirl the plates and allow each drug to spread to the entire surface and let the plates dry at room temperature.
Transfer two- or four-day-old adult transgenic animals on paraquat- or CCCP-containing plates.
Incubate worms at 20°C for microscopic examination after two days of exposure to drugs.
Incubate freshly E. coli (OP50) seeded NGM plates for 30 minutes at 37°C.
Transfer two or four-day-old adult transgenic animals onto pre-warmed plates.
Incubate the animals for two hours at 37°C.
Remove the plates from 37°C and let worms recover for thirty minutes at 20°C.
Collect transgenic animals with an eyebrow/eyelash hair and let them crawl into an empty NGM plate to remove bacteria for five minutes.
Add a droplet of 10 μl M9-levamisole buffer (20 mM final concentration) on a 2% agarose pad.
Collect transgenic animals with an eyebrow/eyelash hair and place them in the M9-levamisole droplet to immobilize the animals for imaging.
Gently place a coverslip on top of the sample.
Samples are ready for microscopic examination with either a Zeiss AxioImager Z2 epifluorescence microscope or a Zeiss AxioObserver Z1 confocal microscope.
Photograph single transgenic animals using a camera attached to the microscope.
Use Zeiss AxioImager Z2 epifluorescence microscope to acquire fluorescent images of whole transgenic animals expressing mtRosella in body wall muscle cells.

Perform z-stack method on an entire single body wall muscle cell co-expressing mitochondria-targeted GFP with autophagosomal marker LGG-1 fused with DsRed using Zeiss AxioObserver Z1 confocal microscope.
Document imaging parameters including lens and magnifier used, filters exposure time, resolution, laser intensity, gain etc.
Save collected images from each method (A or B).
Proceed to image and data analysis.
Process images collected from method A with ImageJ software.
Convert images to a pixel depth of 8 bit (256 shades of grey).
Focus on body wall muscle cells of the head region to avoid intestinal autofluorescence.
Select the "split channel" command via the "image" and "colour" drop-down menu to convert images.
Use the "freehand selection" tool to enclose the fluorescent area.
Select the "measurement" command via the "analyze" drop-down menu to perform pixel intensity analysis.
Normalize pixel intensity values to the selected area using Microsoft Office 2011 Excel software package.
Calculate GFP to DsRed ratio.
Process images collected from method B with Zeiss ZEN 2011 software.
Analyze mitochondria engulfed by autophagosomes manually in each stack of body wall muscle cells.
Count co-localization events between mitochondrial (mtGFP) and autophagosomal marker (LGG-1::DsRed).
Analyze the data using Microsoft Office 2011 Excel software package.
